items.title: 日本10年債殖利率飆破3% 貝森特「逼宮」日本大撒錢 要求升息、收斂財政支出
items.title_en: Japan 10-Year Bond Yield Surges Past 3% as Bessent Pressures Tokyo to Spend Big, Demand Rate Hikes and Fiscal Tightening
paras: 美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)近幾個月持續向日本政府施壓，要求東京控制大規模財政支出、讓日本央行加快升息，以遏制日元疲弱與通膨壓力。路透引述3名知情人士指出，當日本財務大臣片山皐月(Satsuki Katayama)今年6月22日致電貝森特，希望美國協助支撐大幅走貶的日元時，貝森特反而要求日本先處理財政政策問題，並避免貨幣與財政政策相互矛盾。
這通此前未被公開報導的電話，成為美日兩國7月底大規模聯手干預匯市的前奏。日本方面原本擔心日元疲弱推高通膨，進而傷害首相高市早苗的政治支持度；但貝森特更關注日本公債遭大幅拋售可能波及美國公債市場。日本是美國國債最大的海外持有國，因此日本長期公債殖利率若大幅攀升，可能推高美國政府的借貸成本。
貝森特過去數月已私下向片山及其他日本官員表示，日本應收斂大規模財政支出，同時日本央行需要升息。他在6月通話中再次要求東京處理推低日元的根本因素，並認為高市政府擴大支出的政策，正在削弱日本央行抑制通膨的努力。
貝森特5月在日本與片山會面時，也曾強調日本央行需要提高利率。3名消息人士表示，當時日本政府內部已普遍認為6月或7月升息幾乎勢在必行。日本央行6月升息後，片山一度認為貝森特可能同意美國加入聯合買進日元的行動，但貝森特仍把焦點放在日本財政政策。
7月底，美日最終展開聯合干預匯市。日本首席外匯事務官三村淳(Atsushi Mimura)當時形容，這是日本與美國貨幣合作關係的成果。日本財務省與美國財政部的合作，使日元一度明顯反彈，但這波升值並未持續太久。
數周後，日元重新走弱，美國方面對高市政府未能明顯撤回刺激經濟措施感到失望，加上全球公債殖利率同步攀升，使日本財政問題受到更大關注。8月31日至9月1日舉行的G20財長會議上，貝森特再次要求日本升息並收緊財政政策，且語氣較先前更為強硬。
貝森特此前接受媒體訪問時表示，日本應該「坐下來享受安倍經濟學的成功」，理由是日本長期通縮時代已經過去，目前政策重點應從刺激經濟轉向控制通膨。這被視為美國迄今對高市政府延續安倍經濟學政策最明確的警告之一。
隨著市場持續拋售日本公債，日本10年期基準公債殖利率9月初升破3%關卡，觸及30年高點。日本前最高外匯事務官古澤滿宏(Mitsuhiro Furusawa)指出，日本公共債務規模龐大，需要提出可信的中長期財政展望，並確保貨幣政策與財政政策一致，避免長期利率出現不受歡迎的急升。
在G20會議期間，片山向與會財長保證，日本將降低對額外支出的依賴，也不會透過發行債券來支應減稅。她會後透露，自己曾向貝森特展示高市早苗接受日本媒體《讀賣新聞》訪問時提出的「同時實現經濟成長與財政紀律」主張，貝森特則回應表示認同。
貝森特隨後再度對日元空頭發出警告，並表示自己掌握部分日本政策制定者包括日本央行的非對稱資訊，對政策走向具有較深入的了解。他甚至表示「現在我是莊家」，並稱投資人如果願意可以押注與他相反的方向，相關言論也一度帶動日元升值。
這場美日財政與貨幣政策角力，正值日本央行準備進一步升息之際。日本央行的政策方向大致與貝森特要求提高利率的立場一致，但在財政政策方面，日本政府與美國之間仍存在明顯落差。
高市早苗很難完全撤回帶動其所屬政黨在今年選舉中取得支持的主要刺激政策。政府透過補貼及其他措施降低燃料成本，也有助於緩解民眾對生活成本上升的不滿，因此大幅削減支出可能帶來政治壓力。
另一方面，美國若要求日本大幅縮減減稅與支出計畫，也可能削弱一個重要亞洲盟友的政府穩定性。在美國與中國競爭升溫之際，華府仍重視與日本的安全及經濟合作。美國總統川普在美日共同支撐日元後，也再次強調兩國夥伴關係的重要性。
日本政府周四進行內閣改組，高市早苗重新任命片山皐月擔任財務大臣，被部分市場人士視為兼顧市場信心與政策延續性的安排。片山本身較偏向財政保守立場，近來一方面需要向市場保證日本不會無限制擴大支出，另一方面也必須推動高市政府的投資與經濟政策。
不過，目前並沒有跡象顯示高市政府準備全面放棄擴張性財政政策。日本下一財政年度的預算要求總額已膨脹至143兆日元(約9,161.4億美元)，接近疫情期間的高峰。高市政府則承諾，在截至2028年3月的財政年度，新發行公債規模將維持約40兆日元，高於本年度預估的32.7兆日元。
部分日本官員認為，若考量臨時調降消費稅、增加國防支出以及融資成本上升，要將新發債規模控制在40兆日元左右可能相當困難。日本政府近期公布的食品消費稅減免計畫本身就可能造成約5兆日元的稅收缺口，進一步增加市場對財政健全性的疑慮。
目前這場財政政策僵局尚未演變成更大規模的美日衝突，顯示高市政府與川普政府之間仍保有一定外交空間。不過，部分分析人士認為，貝森特對日本財政政策的施壓，反映川普政府正在把其對盟友的談判方式延伸至金融與財政政策領域。
日本前外匯官員中尾武彥(Takehiko Nakao)表示，美國過去對日本的訊息較偏向要求東京採取正確政策，如今則顯得更直接。美國關切的不只是日元匯率，也包括日本公債市場穩定、通膨政策可信度，以及日本大量持有美國國債對美國融資成本可能造成的影響。
因此，貝森特與日本政府之間的角力已不再只是單純的匯率問題，而是同時牽涉日本央行升息速度、政府支出、減稅、國防預算、日本公債殖利率，以及全球最大兩個政府債券市場之間的相互影響。對高市政府而言，如何在維持經濟刺激政策、控制生活成本與回應金融市場對財政紀律的要求之間取得平衡，將成為後續政策的核心課題。
paras_en: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been pressing the Japanese government for months, urging Tokyo to curb massive fiscal spending and accelerate rate hikes by the Bank of Japan to curb a weak yen and inflation pressures. Reuters, citing three informed sources, said that when Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama called Bessent on June 22 to ask for U.S. support for the sharply depreciating yen, Bessent instead told Japan to first address its fiscal policy issues and avoid contradictions between monetary and fiscal policy.

The previously undisclosed call set the stage for the large‑scale joint FX intervention by the United States and Japan at the end of July. Japan had feared that a weak yen would lift inflation and erode Prime Minister Kishida Nae‑suke’s political support, but Bessent was more worried that a heavy sell‑off of Japanese government bonds could spill over into the U.S. Treasury market. Japan is the largest foreign holder of U.S. Treasuries, so a sharp rise in Japanese long‑term bond yields could push up borrowing costs for the U.S. government.

Bessent has privately told Katayama and other Japanese officials over the past few months that Japan should rein in its massive fiscal outlays while the BOJ needs to raise rates. In the June call he again urged Tokyo to tackle the root causes of yen weakness and argued that the Kishida administration’s expansionary spending was undermining the BOJ’s fight against inflation.

When Bessent met Katayama in Japan in May, he also stressed that the BOJ needed to hike rates. Three sources said that at the time the Japanese government already believed a rate hike in June or July was almost inevitable. After the BOJ raised rates in June, Katayama briefly thought Bessent might agree to a joint yen‑buying operation, but Bessent kept the focus on Japan’s fiscal stance.

At the end of July the U.S. and Japan carried out a joint FX intervention. Japan’s chief foreign exchange official Atsushi Mimura described it as the fruit of monetary cooperation between the two countries. The coordination between Japan’s finance ministry and the U.S. Treasury sparked a noticeable yen rally, but the appreciation was short‑lived.

Weeks later the yen weakened again. The United States expressed disappointment that the Kishida government had not rolled back its stimulus measures, and rising global bond yields heightened scrutiny of Japan’s fiscal situation. At the G20 finance ministers’ meeting on Aug. 31‑Sept. 1, Bessent again demanded that Japan raise rates and tighten fiscal policy, using a tougher tone than before.

In a prior media interview Bessent said Japan should “sit down and enjoy the success of Abenomics,” arguing that the era of chronic deflation is over and policy should shift from stimulus to inflation control. The comment was seen as one of the clearest U.S. warnings to the Kishida administration about continuing Abenomics‑style policies.

As markets kept selling Japanese bonds, the yield on the benchmark 10‑year Japanese government bond broke the 3% barrier in early September, hitting a 30‑year high. Former top FX official Mitsuhiro Furusawa warned that Japan’s huge public debt requires a credible medium‑ to long‑term fiscal outlook and alignment of monetary and fiscal policy to avoid an unwelcome surge in long‑term rates.

During the G20 meeting Katayama assured fellow finance chiefs that Japan would reduce reliance on extra spending and would not fund tax cuts by issuing new bonds. After the meeting she disclosed that she had shown Bessent Kishida’s “grow the economy while maintaining fiscal discipline” pitch given to Yomiuri Shimbun, which Bessent said he agreed with.

Bessent later warned yen short‑sellers again, claiming he possessed asymmetric information about Japanese policymakers, including the BOJ, giving him deeper insight into policy direction. He even said, “Now I am the house,” and suggested investors could bet against him, a remark that briefly boosted the yen.

The U.S.–Japan clash over fiscal and monetary policy comes as the BOJ prepares to raise rates further. The BOJ’s policy trajectory broadly aligns with Bessent’s call for higher rates, but a gap remains on the fiscal side between Japan’s government and Washington.

Kishida finds it hard to fully roll back the stimulus measures that have helped his party gain electoral support this year. Subsidies and other actions that lower fuel costs ease public anger over rising living expenses, so a sharp cut in spending could create political pressure.

Conversely, if the United States demands a major cut in Japan’s tax cuts and spending plans, it could undermine the stability of an important Asian ally. With U.S.–China competition heating up, Washington still values Japan’s security and economic partnership. After the joint effort to support the yen, President Trump again stressed the importance of the bilateral partnership.

Japan reshuffled its cabinet on Thursday, re‑appointing Katayama as finance minister under Kishida, a move some market participants saw as balancing market confidence with policy continuity. Katayama leans fiscally conservative and now must reassure markets that Japan will not expand spending unchecked while still advancing Kishida’s investment and economic agenda.

Nevertheless, there is no sign that the Kishida administration is ready to abandon its expansionary fiscal stance. The budget request for the next fiscal year has swelled to ¥143 trillion (about $9.16 billion), near the pandemic‑era peak. The government has pledged that new bond issuance for the fiscal year ending March 2028 will stay around ¥40 trillion, above the current‑year estimate of ¥32.7 trillion.

Some officials argue that, given a temporary cut to the consumption tax, higher defence spending and rising financing costs, keeping new issuance near ¥40 trillion will be very difficult. The recently announced food‑tax relief plan could create a ¥5 trillion revenue gap, further raising doubts about fiscal soundness.

The fiscal standoff has not yet escalated into a broader U.S.–Japan clash, indicating that diplomatic space remains between the Kishida and Trump administrations. However, some analysts say Bessent’s pressure on Japan’s fiscal policy reflects the Trump administration’s habit of extending its negotiating style with allies into financial and fiscal realms.

Former FX official Takehiko Nakao said the United States used to mainly tell Tokyo to adopt the right policies, but now its messaging is more direct. Washington’s concerns cover not only the yen rate but also the stability of Japan’s bond market, the credibility of its inflation policy and the impact of Japan’s large U.S. Treasury holdings on U.S. financing costs.

Thus the contest between Bessent and the Japanese government is no longer just about exchange rates; it also involves BOJ rate‑hike speed, government spending, tax cuts, defence budgeting, Japanese bond yields and the interaction of the world’s two largest sovereign‑debt markets. For Kishida’s government, balancing economic stimulus, cost‑of‑living pressures and market demands for fiscal discipline will be the core policy challenge going forward.

items.title: 植田談話恐令市場失望？日銀利率決議出爐前夕　富國銀行高調做空日元、花旗估將跌向159
items.title_en: Will Ueda's Remarks Disappoint the Market? On the Eve of the BOJ Rate Decision, Wells Fargo Shorts the Yen Aggressively, Citi Forecasts a Drop to 159
paras: 日本央行(BOJ)公布最新利率決議前夕，外匯策略師普遍預期「升息容易、表態難鷹」，日元短線偏向貶值。掉期市場數據幾乎完全計入升息1碼，焦點轉向BOJ總裁植田和男記者會對後續節奏的指引。日元在今日亞洲匯市早盤小貶約0.1%至156.15。
富國銀行策略師Chidu Narayanan表示，BOJ要達到甚至超越市場鷹派預期「門檻​​很高」，會議結果若僅兌現升息、不明示連續緊縮，風險傾向偏鴿，建議做空日元。
ING Bank NV的G10外匯策略主管Chris Turner預估，若BOJ未能釋放進一步升息訊號，日元兌美元將貶至157或158水平，花旗策略師Daniel Tobon更預估未來幾週日元可能貶向159。
壓低日元反彈的是美日利差。聯準會(Fed)週三宣布升息1碼至3.75%—4%，主席華許暗示通膨偏高、必要時繼續收緊，美元指數站上100，美債短端利率走高，
不過，策略師們對中長線判斷分化；花旗認為日本近期匯率與貨幣政策調整屬「制度轉變」一部分，長期仍利於日元；荷蘭銀行資深外匯策略師Georgette Boele則預期能源價格暫時抑制反彈，2027年第一季前美元兌日元將在154附近交易，2027下半年隨Fed、歐洲央行(ECB)降息才轉強。整體來看，短線市場以「鴿派升息」防日元回貶，158—160為關鍵觀察區。
paras_en: Ahead of the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) latest rate decision, most FX strategists expect a "rate hike is easy, hawkish guidance is hard," implying short‑term yen weakness. Swap market data almost fully priced in a 10‑basis‑point hike, shifting focus to the guidance on future pacing from BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda's press conference. The yen slipped about 0.1% to 156.15 in early Asian trading today.

Wells Fargo strategist Chidu Narayanan said the BOJ faces a very high hurdle to meet or exceed market hawkish expectations. If the meeting only delivers a hike without signalling further tightening, the bias leans dovish, so he recommends shorting the yen.

ING Bank NV’s G10 FX strategy head Chris Turner projected that if the BOJ fails to signal additional hikes, the yen will fall to the 157‑158 level against the dollar, while Citi strategist Daniel Tobon sees the yen possibly sliding toward 159 in the coming weeks.

The yen’s downside is being capped by the US‑Japan rate differential. The Fed raised rates by one quarter point on Wednesday to a 3.75%‑4% range, with Chair Powell hinting that inflation remains elevated and further tightening may be needed. The dollar index is above 100 and short‑term US Treasury yields are rising.

However, strategists diverge on the medium‑to‑long term. Citi views Japan’s recent exchange‑rate and policy moves as part of a "structural shift" that will ultimately benefit the yen, while senior ING FX strategist Georgette Boele expects energy prices to temporarily suppress a rebound, forecasting the dollar‑yen around 154 before Q1 2027 and only strengthening in the second half of 2027 after rate cuts by the Fed and ECB. Overall, the short‑term market is watching the "dovish hike" narrative to prevent a yen rebound, with 158‑160 as the key observation zone.

items.title: QUANTRON、HyperView結盟攻零排放商用車 鴻海成關鍵製造夥伴
items.title_en: QUANTRON and HyperView Team Up to Attack Zero‑Emission Commercial Vehicles, Foxconn Becomes Key Manufacturing Partner
paras: 德國QUANTRON與中國HyperView宣布成立「QUANTRON China」，鴻海(2317-TW)將擔任卡車與巴士平台的工業製造夥伴，雙方將結合德國工程技術、自動駕駛、中國工業生態及鴻海製造能力，推動次世代零排放與智慧商用車全球布局。
根據合作計劃，鴻海將提供卡車與巴士平台的工業製造能力，結合可擴充的國際SKD製造模式、工業化供應鏈與生產成本優勢，計劃目標於2026年底前將首批100輛車投入歐洲客戶日常營運，並作為2027年上半年全球首發的QUANTRON Gen2技術橋樑與驗證車隊。
QUANTRON表示，QUANTRON China將以中國為製造基地，服務中國市場的同時，支援QUANTRON拓展歐洲、中東等國際市場，並計劃在中國紹興建立零排放商用移動、智慧車輛技術及未來自動駕駛運輸解決方案的國際中心。
本次合作核心QUANTRON Gen2商用車平台，將結合雙方在零排放車輛、自動駕駛、數位智慧及智慧車輛架構等技術，支援純電動及氫燃料電池卡車、巴士，並導入新一代駕駛艙、空氣動力學、智慧聯網及數位車隊管理功能，為未來自動駕駛能力奠定基礎。
HyperView已交付數百輛氫燃料電池商用車，主要分布於中國，並已部署首批車輛至沙烏地阿拉伯；QUANTRON則已將數百輛零排放車輛與系統推向市場，客戶及專案遍及歐洲與中東，近期也在巴西交付氫能車輛。
此外，QUANTRON透過「Quantron-as-a-Service（QaaS）」模式推動零排放商用車規模化，整合車輛、金融融資、售後服務、維修保養、出勤率保證、數位車隊管理及能源解決方案，以降低客戶導入零排放車輛的前期投資負擔，目標未來10年將建構可支援全球超過10萬輛零排放商用車的生態系統。
paras_en: German QUANTRON and China’s HyperView announced the formation of “QUANTRON China,” with Foxconn (2317‑TW) serving as the industrial manufacturing partner for truck and bus platforms. The two will combine German engineering, autonomous driving technology, China’s industrial ecosystem, and Foxconn’s manufacturing capabilities to drive a global rollout of next‑generation zero‑emission and smart commercial vehicles.

Under the cooperation plan, Foxconn will provide industrial manufacturing capacity for truck and bus platforms, leveraging a scalable international SKD production model, an industrialized supply chain and cost advantages. The goal is to deliver the first 100 vehicles to European customers for daily operation by the end of 2026, and to use them as the bridge and validation fleet for QUANTRON’s Gen2 technology slated for a global launch in the first half of 2027.

QUANTRON said QUANTRON China will use China as its manufacturing base, serving the domestic market while supporting QUANTRON’s expansion into Europe, the Middle East and other international markets. It also plans to establish an international centre in Shaoxing, China, for zero‑emission commercial mobility, smart‑vehicle technology and future autonomous‑driving transport solutions.

The core of the collaboration is the QUANTRON Gen2 commercial‑vehicle platform, which will integrate both parties’ expertise in zero‑emission vehicles, autonomous driving, digital intelligence and smart‑vehicle architecture. It will support pure‑electric and hydrogen‑fuel‑cell trucks and buses, and will feature a next‑generation cockpit, aerodynamics, smart connectivity and digital fleet‑management functions to lay the groundwork for future autonomous capabilities.

HyperView has already delivered hundreds of hydrogen‑fuel‑cell commercial vehicles, mainly in China, and has deployed its first batch of vehicles to Saudi Arabia. QUANTRON has likewise brought hundreds of zero‑emission vehicles and systems to market, with customers and projects across Europe and the Middle East, and recently delivered hydrogen vehicles in Brazil.

In addition, QUANTRON is promoting the scaling of zero‑emission commercial vehicles through its “Quantron‑as‑a‑Service (QaaS)” model, which integrates vehicles, financing, after‑sales service, maintenance, uptime guarantees, digital fleet management and energy solutions to reduce the upfront investment burden for customers. The aim is to build an ecosystem capable of supporting over 100,000 zero‑emission commercial vehicles worldwide within the next ten years.

items.title: 泰福CDMO與澳洲Q-Sera簽訂長期供貨協議 攜手打入日本醫材廠供應鏈
items.title_en: Tai Fu CDMO signs long-term supply agreement with Australia's Q‑Sera, jointly entering Japanese medical device supply chain
paras: 泰福(6541-TW)旗下生物製劑CDMO品牌Bora Biologics宣布，與澳洲採血管技術公司Q-Sera簽訂長期供貨協議，供應重組RAPClot蛋白，並打入Q-Sera與日本醫療器材廠泰爾茂(Terumo)商業化合作供應鏈，實現VenoJect II RAPClot真空採血管於日本上市。
泰福指出，Bora Biologics竹北廠自有細胞株技術與重組蛋白製造專業，符合Q-Sera要求，因此於2021年開始協助Q-Sera進行RAPClot的開發與製程放大。在4年內製程成功放大至商業化生產規模後，雙方簽訂長期供貨合約，支援泰爾茂的商業化進程。

paras_en: Tai Fu (6541‑TW) subsidiary biopharmaceutical CDMO brand Bora Biologics announced that it has signed a long‑term supply agreement with Australian blood‑tube technology company Q‑Sera to supply recombinant RAPClot protein, and to enter the commercialization partnership supply chain between Q‑Sera and Japanese medical device manufacturer Terumo, enabling the VenoJect II RAPClot vacuum blood‑collection tube to be launched in Japan.

Tai Fu noted that Bora Biologics’ Zhubei plant, with its proprietary cell‑line technology and expertise in recombinant protein manufacturing, meets Q‑Sera’s requirements; therefore, since 2021 it has been assisting Q‑Sera in the development and scale‑up of RAPClot. After successfully scaling the process to commercial production capacity within four years, the two parties signed a long‑term supply contract to support Terumo’s commercialization efforts.

Tai Fu further stated that Terumo has obtained exclusive authorization from Q‑Sera to launch the product in Japan. RAPClot can rapidly generate serum for biochemical testing, even from blood samples containing anticoagulants, helping to shorten turnaround time and improve laboratory efficiency.

4. • Polyester Fiber (autumn‑winter inventory buildup and margin recovery): European and American apparel inventories have largely been cleared, prompting a rebound in upstream polyester raw‑material orders. paras_en: U.S. equities all rose on Thursday (the 17th), with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumping 3.14%. The Nasdaq closed up 1.69%, the S&P 500 gained 1.14% and the Dow slipped 0.61%. The seven big tech names all moved higher – Nvidia, Tesla and Amazon each rose more than 2%, while Microsoft, Apple, Meta and Google each added over 1%.

AI hardware and semiconductor stocks led the gains. Arm surged more than 8%, Intel climbed over 7%, and SanDisk and AMD each rose more than 6%. Micron jumped over 5%, SK Hynix, Dell and Marvell each added more than 4%, and Seagate and Qualcomm were up over 2%. In the optical‑communications sector performance was mixed: Marvell, Corning and Coherent each rose more than 2% while Lumentum fell nearly 3%. Cloud‑AI compute provider CoreWeave dropped more than 4% after it announced a $3 billion private placement of convertible preferred notes due 2033, with the initial investors allowed to add $500 million and the company planning to issue up to 35 million Class A shares via an ATM, sparking concerns about dilution and bond‑conversion dilution.

Chinese‑listed U.S. stocks showed mixed results. The Golden Dragon Index inched up 0.16%. HaiChuan Securities jumped 25%, Burning Rock Medical rose close to 8%, Pony.ai surged over 5%, BYD ADR gained more than 3%, while Bilibili, Meituan ADR and Pinduoduo were weaker.

At the same time, the Middle‑East situation added a new variable. According to a recent report by Axios, former President Donald Trump is weighing whether to restart a large‑scale offensive against Iran and plans to meet leaders of six Persian Gulf countries during next week’s United Nations General Assembly to decide on diplomatic de‑escalation or a military escalation.

Some U.S. officials warned that the U.S.–Iran clash is stuck in a “neither war nor peace” stalemate and that, if negotiations fail, a large‑scale operation could resume after the midterm elections. Falling oil prices and expectations of military escalation are pulling in opposite directions, likely continuing to affect the pricing of energy, gold and technology stocks.

items.title: QUANTRON、HyperView結盟攻零排放商用車 鴻海成關鍵製造夥伴
items.title_en: QUANTRON and HyperView Team Up to Attack Zero‑Emission Commercial Vehicles, Foxconn Becomes Key Manufacturing Partner
paras: 德國QUANTRON與中國HyperView宣布成立「QUANTRON China」，鴻海(2317-TW)將擔任卡車與巴士平台的工業製造夥伴，雙方將結合德國工程技術、自動駕駛、中國工業生態及鴻海製造能力，推動次世代零排放與智慧商用車全球布局。
根據合作計劃，鴻海將提供卡車與巴士平台的工業製造能力，結合可擴充的國際SKD製造模式、工業化供應鏈與生產成本優勢，計劃目標於2026年底前將首批100輛車投入歐洲客戶日常營運，並作為2027年上半年全球首發的QUANTRON Gen2技術橋樑與驗證車隊。
QUANTRON表示，QUANTRON China將以中國為製造基地，服務中國市場的同時，支援QUANTRON拓展歐洲、中東等國際市場，並計劃在中國紹興建立零排放商用移動、智慧車輛技術及未來自動駕駛運輸解決方案的國際中心。
本次合作核心QUANTRON Gen2商用車平台，將結合雙方在零排放車輛、自動駕駛、數位智慧及智慧車輛架構等技術，支援純電動及氫燃料電池卡車、巴士，並導入新一代駕駛艙、空氣動力學、智慧聯網及數位車隊管理功能，為未來自動駕駛能力奠定基礎。
HyperView已交付數百輛氫燃料電池商用車，主要分布於中國，並已部署首批車輛至沙烏地阿拉伯；QUANTRON則已將數百輛零排放車輛與系統推向市場，客戶及專案遍及歐洲與中東，近期也在巴西交付氫能車輛。
此外，QUANTRON透過「Quantron-as-a-Service（QaaS）」模式推動零排放商用車規模化，整合車輛、金融融資、售後服務、維修保養、出勤率保證、數位車隊管理及能源解決方案，以降低客戶導入零排放車輛的前期投資負擔，目標未來10年將建構可支援全球超過10萬輛零排放商用車的生態系統。
paras_en: German QUANTRON and China’s HyperView announced the formation of “QUANTRON China,” with Foxconn (2317‑TW) serving as the industrial manufacturing partner for truck and bus platforms. The two will combine German engineering, autonomous driving technology, China’s industrial ecosystem, and Foxconn’s manufacturing capabilities to drive a global rollout of next‑generation zero‑emission and smart commercial vehicles.

Under the cooperation plan, Foxconn will provide industrial manufacturing capacity for truck and bus platforms, leveraging a scalable international SKD production model, an industrialized supply chain and cost advantages. The goal is to deliver the first 100 vehicles to European customers for daily operation by the end of 2026, and to use them as the bridge and validation fleet for QUANTRON’s Gen2 technology slated for a global launch in the first half of 2027.

QUANTRON said QUANTRON China will use China as its manufacturing base, serving the domestic market while supporting QUANTRON’s expansion into Europe, the Middle East and other international markets. It also plans to establish an international centre in Shaoxing, China, for zero‑emission commercial mobility, smart‑vehicle technology and future autonomous‑driving transport solutions.

The core of the collaboration is the QUANTRON Gen2 commercial‑vehicle platform, which will integrate both parties’ expertise in zero‑emission vehicles, autonomous driving, digital intelligence and smart‑vehicle architecture. It will support pure‑electric and hydrogen‑fuel‑cell trucks and buses, and will feature a next‑generation cockpit, aerodynamics, smart connectivity and digital fleet‑management functions to lay the groundwork for future autonomous capabilities.

HyperView has already delivered hundreds of hydrogen‑fuel‑cell commercial vehicles, mainly in China, and has deployed its first batch of vehicles to Saudi Arabia. QUANTRON has likewise brought hundreds of zero‑emission vehicles and systems to market, with customers and projects across Europe and the Middle East, and recently delivered hydrogen vehicles in Brazil.

In addition, QUANTRON is promoting the scaling of zero‑emission commercial vehicles through its “Quantron‑as‑a‑Service (QaaS)” model, which integrates vehicles, financing, after‑sales service, maintenance, uptime guarantees, digital fleet management and energy solutions to reduce the upfront investment burden for customers. The aim is to build an ecosystem capable of supporting over 100,000 zero‑emission commercial vehicles worldwide within the next ten years.

items.title: 泰福CDMO與澳洲Q-Sera簽訂長期供貨協議 攜手打入日本醫材廠供應鏈
items.title_en: Tai Fu CDMO signs long-term supply agreement with Australia's Q‑Sera, jointly entering Japanese medical device supply chain
paras: 泰福(6541-TW)旗下生物製劑CDMO品牌Bora Biologics宣布，與澳洲採血管技術公司Q-Sera簽訂長期供貨協議，供應重組RAPClot蛋白，並打入Q-Sera與日本醫療器材廠泰爾茂(Terumo)商業化合作供應鏈，實現VenoJect II RAPClot真空採血管於日本上市。
泰福指出，Bora Biologics竹北廠自有細胞株技術與重組蛋白製造專業，符合Q-Sera要求，因此於2021年開始協助Q-Sera進行RAPClot的開發與製程放大。在4年內製程成功放大至商業化生產規模後，雙方簽訂長期供貨合約，支援泰爾茂的商業化進程。
泰福進一步指出，泰爾默獲Q-Sera獨家授權在日本推出此產品，RAPClot可快速產出供生化檢驗使用的血清，即便是含抗凝血劑的血液檢體也適用，有助縮短檢驗周轉時間，提升實驗室效率。
paras_en: Tai Fu (6541‑TW) subsidiary biopharmaceutical CDMO brand Bora Biologics announced that it has signed a long‑term supply agreement with Australian blood‑tube technology company Q‑Sera to supply recombinant RAPClot protein, and to enter the commercialization partnership supply chain between Q‑Sera and Japanese medical device manufacturer Terumo, enabling the VenoJect II RAPClot vacuum blood‑collection tube to be launched in Japan.

Tai Fu noted that Bora Biologics’ Zhubei plant, with its proprietary cell‑line technology and expertise in recombinant protein manufacturing, meets Q‑Sera’s requirements; therefore, since 2021 it has been assisting Q‑Sera in the development and scale‑up of RAPClot. After successfully scaling the process to commercial production capacity within four years, the two parties signed a long‑term supply contract to support Terumo’s commercialization efforts.

Tai Fu further stated that Terumo has obtained exclusive authorization from Q‑Sera to launch the product in Japan. RAPClot can rapidly generate serum for biochemical testing, even from blood samples containing anticoagulants, helping to shorten turnaround time and improve laboratory efficiency.

2. On the previous trading day (9/17) the Taiwan market was led higher by the heavyweight TSMC (2330), which jumped NT$45.00 (+1.89%). Together with strong gains in Formosa Plastics’ four core stocks, UMC (2303), Creative (3443) and other blue‑chip stocks, the market displayed a broad‑based rally. (6505) rose NT$5.70 to NT$86.20 (+7.08%) and Creative surged NT$330.00 to NT$6,500.00 (+5.35%). The three main institutional groups in the main board bought a net NT$21.5 billion, with foreign investors net‑buying about NT$12.2 billion, investment trusts about NT$7.7 billion and dealers about NT$1.6 billion. The OTC index rose to 407.80 points in the morning but was pulled back in the afternoon by selling pressure in high‑priced electronic components, ending down 1.04 points (-0.26%) at 398.17 with turnover around NT$261.9 billion, staying above its 5‑day and quarterly averages. Across the whole market, institutions net‑bought roughly NT$10.5 billion (foreign investors about NT$1.1 billion, dealers about NT$4.1 billion, and investment trusts about NT$5.3 billion).
3. Strong Sectors

4. • Polyester Fiber (autumn‑winter inventory buildup and margin recovery): European and American apparel inventories have largely been cleared, prompting a rebound in upstream polyester raw‑material orders. Ethylene glycol (EG) and PTA prices are supported by petrochemical plants cutting output to protect prices. Dong Lian (1710) surged +6.05% to NT$16.65, Li Li (1444) rose +4.78% to NT$7.01, Nan Fang (1440) gained +4.26% to NT$13.45, Xin Xian (1409) climbed +3.55% to NT$24.80 and Far Eastern New (1402) steadied up +2.55% to NT$28.10.

5. • Plastic Feedstock (high crude oil support and improving autumn supply‑demand balance): Spot prices for general‑purpose resin have rebounded sharply as Asian cracking plants enter their seasonal maintenance cycle. Formosa Plastics’ four core stocks led the rally: Taiwan Benzene (1310) jumped +6.36% to NT$9.03, Nan Ya (1303) surged on huge volume +5.36% to NT$236.00, Taiwan Chemical (1326) rose +4.26% to NT$68.60, Formosa Plastics (1301) climbed +3.53% to NT$64.60, while Huaxia (1305) and Lian Cheng (1313) both advanced +2.93% to NT$12.30.

6. • Container Shipping (tight negotiations at East Coast U.S. ports and strong year‑end replenishment season): Negotiations over contracts at East Coast terminals have triggered a scramble for space, and the Red Sea detour around the Cape of Good Hope has helped absorb excess capacity. Loading rates on East and West Coast U.S. routes remained near full in Q4. 8. • Copper‑Foil Substrates (CCL) (short‑term gains exhausted and server‑production transition noise): After previously benefiting from AI‑driven demand for high‑frequency, high‑speed materials, the sector faced sharp profit‑taking pressure at elevated levels. Lian Mao (6213) hit the limit down, closing at NT$495.00 (-10.00%). Index component Tai Guang Dian (2383) plunged -7.67% to NT$4,695.00, Tai Yao (6274) fell -6.71% to NT$1,320.00 and Teng Hui Electronics‑KY (6672) dropped -3.45% to NT$293.50.

9. • Glass Fiber Cloth (downstream CCL volatility and stop‑loss selling): As a key upstream substrate material, the downstream slump raised concerns about slowing demand for high‑grade low‑Dk glass fiber yarn. De Hong (5475) slid -5.77% to NT$171.50, Fu Qiao (1815) fell over -5.49% to NT$112.00, Jian Rong (5340) declined -2.98% to NT$81.50, while only Taiwan Glass (1802) managed to hold flat at NT$58.50.

10. • Upstream Materials for Printed Circuit Boards (short‑term over‑extension correction): Consumables such as drill bits and metal copper foil retreated as electronic capital rotated out. paras_en: Taiwan Stock Market Pre‑Market News

1. The Taiwan index closed at 46,288 points on the 17th, up 439.1 points, reclaiming the 46,000‑point threshold. Turnover rose to NT$819.405 billion, with foreign investors switching from net selling to net buying, netting a purchase of NT$12.185 billion. Their biggest buys were 53,000 shares of AU Optronics and 33,000 shares of Powerchip Semiconductor. The four major U.S. indices rallied sharply during the session, and Taiwan futures jumped nearly 700 points in after‑hours trading, briefly reaching 47,161 points. TSMC ADR (TSM‑US) rose more than 2%.

2. Although the U.S. Federal Reserve just announced a 25‑basis‑point rate hike, whether Taiwan will follow has sparked debate domestically. The Central Bank held its policy rate steady at the “10‑year freeze” during its Q3 board meeting on the 17th, with Governor Yang Jin‑long saying, “We will walk our own path.” At the same time, the bank relaxed selective credit controls on the housing market, raising the maximum loan‑to‑value ratio for a second home from 60% to 70%.

3. On the 17th, the Central Bank raised its forecast for Taiwan’s second‑half GDP growth to 9.09%, lifting the full‑year GDP estimate to 11.48%. It projects next year’s GDP at 5.82%. Inflation forecasts were also upgraded, with this year’s CPI and core‑CPI annual growth now expected at 2.03% and 2.16% respectively, indicating price pressures remain above the 2% warning line.

4. The Central Bank’s decision to ease housing‑market controls surprised the market. Governor Yang said only one board member opposed the relaxation. He explained that the bank wants the market to know “the central bank is not rigid,” and that “relevant firms must also consider their sentiment,” and that the bank will continue a rolling review of market developments.

5. Sinopec Corp. (1314‑TW) Chairman Ge Shuren said the company has been gradually reducing its traditional petrochemical exposure and focusing on high‑value materials, new energy, AI‑driven high‑speed communications, and semiconductor materials as new growth engines. Sinopec is also evaluating the construction of AI data centers. The firm will cooperate with external partners to build an AI compute center; the first phase is expected to have a 5 MW capacity and a total investment of NT$2 billion.

6. Optics component maker Largan Precision (3008‑TW) continued its land‑acquisition spree after buying plots in the Taichung Industrial Zone, now purchasing industrial real estate in the Precision Machinery Park. On the 17th, Largan announced a NT$1.172 billion acquisition of land and buildings in the park from Taiwan Solid‑State Industrial. The purchase includes 2,259.25 ping of land and 3,695.25 ping of building space, intended to expand production capacity.
7. Post‑market recap: TSMC and Formosa Plastics’ “Four Treasures” all rallied, lifting the index by 439 points to retake the 46,000 level and the monthly moving average.

8. After five consecutive days of net selling, foreign investors reversed course, net buying NT$12.1 billion, heavily purchasing 53,000 shares of AU Optronics and 33,000 shares of Powerchip Semiconductor.
9. The policy rate remains frozen at the “10‑year level,” and housing‑market credit rules are loosened. Governor Yang says Taiwan will not follow the U.S. rate hikes: “We walk our own road.”
10. Inflation is slightly above the warning zone. Governor Yang notes there is still time to observe, and monetary policy remains relatively tight.
11. Discussing the housing‑market easing, Governor Yang said the central bank is not “hard‑nosed” about choking the market and is taking industry sentiment into account.
12. Ericsson partners with MediaTek to improve 5G positioning accuracy, accelerating applications in autonomous vehicles, drones, and smart manufacturing.
13. The New Taiwan dollar rises alongside equities; the “five‑day black” streak ends with a closing rate of NT$31.881 per US$.
14. Largan Precision again spends NT$1.172 billion to acquire land and factory space in Taichung’s Precision Machinery Park.
15. The Fair Trade Commission formally accepted Taiwan‑Da’s public tender offer for Jing Cheng, at a premium of 38%.
16. BlackRock’s survey shows Taiwan ETF penetration at 53% in Greater Asia‑Pacific, with next‑year allocation intent soaring to 74%.
17. Sinopec pushes its transformation into the AI market, projecting the first‑phase compute‑center investment to reach NT$2 billion.

paras_en: September 18, 2026 (U-Analysis/Industry Data Center report) – After the Federal Reserve raised rates by one basis point, U.S. equities rebounded sharply on Thursday, with the Nasdaq climbing 1.7% back above its 50‑day moving average and retaking the 10‑day and 21‑day averages; the S&P 500 rose 1.1% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.6%. Bond yields also fell, easing valuation pressure on growth stocks. The U.S. 10‑year Treasury yield slipped more than six basis points to 4.94%. Nasdaq trading volume increased versus the previous session, and the number of advancing stocks was more than twice the number of decliners, indicating the bounce was not limited to a few large‑cap tech names.

AI data‑center power equipment stocks showed an even stronger reaction. Generac Holdings (GNRC‑US) jumped 18%, becoming the top performer in the S&P 500, after the company signed a long‑term agreement to supply generators to Amazon’s data centers.

This development aligns with the recent trend of power‑supply needs for AI data centers. As data‑center construction outpaces grid expansion in some regions, demand for on‑site generation and downstream power‑delivery equipment is rising rapidly.

paras_en: September 18, 2026 (U-Analysis/Industry Data Center Report) – A large order for AI data‑center power equipment has emerged again. Backup power equipment maker Generac Holdings (GNRC-US) disclosed a $2.4 billion agreement with Amazon (AMZN-US) to supply generators for Amazon’s data centers. The news sent Generac’s stock up more than 18% on Thursday, making it the best‑performing S&P 500 stock of the day, while Amazon rose 2.1%.

The significance of the $2.4 billion contract lies in the fact that AI data‑center power demand is now translating into actual equipment purchases. Recent market activity has seen orders for on‑site generation ranging from hundreds of megawatts to gigawatt scale, reflecting that large tech firms are expanding AI compute capacity while simultaneously increasing procurement of generators and power infrastructure.

On the same day, AI‑infrastructure‑related stocks showed mixed performance. Neocloud provider Nebius (NBIS-US) rose 4.1% after the company recently raised on‑demand rental prices for several AI chips, including roughly a 20% increase for some NVIDIA (NVDA-US) GPUs. IREN (IREN-US) gained 2%, while CoreWeave (CRWV-US) fell 4.2% after announcing a $3 billion convertible bond issuance.

In semiconductors, Arm Holdings (ARM-US) jumped 8.6%. CEO Rene Haas said the company’s confidence has grown in securing sufficient supply to meet a $2 billion data‑center chip demand. AMD (AMD-US), Intel (INTC-US), Marvell Technology (MRVL-US), Coherent (COHR-US), Corning (GLW-US) and SanDisk (SNDK-US) also moved higher.

By contrast, energy‑storage firm Fluence Energy (FLNC-US) slid more than 15% after a delay in ramp‑up at its outsourced manufacturing plant in Houston forced a sharp downward revision of its FY 2026 revenue outlook. The divergent stock reactions underscore that the key issue for AI power infrastructure is no longer just demand, but whether suppliers can convert that demand into capacity, deliver on time and generate real revenue.

AI demand remains robust, and SpaceX (SPCX‑US) shares rose again on Thursday, up 2.6% to $154.81 after a 5.2% jump on Wednesday. The company’s plan to conduct the 14th test flight of its fully reusable Starship rocket may have further boosted the stock.

items.title: 費半漲超3%！美科技股強彈 ARM飆逾8%、閃迪漲超6% 川普擬對伊朗恢復大規模作戰
items.title_en: PHLX Semiconductor Index Up Over 3% – US Tech Stocks Rally as ARM Soars More Than 8%, SanDisk Gains Over 6%, Trump Mulls Resuming Large‑Scale Operations Against Iran
paras: 美股三大指數周四(17日)集體收漲，費城半導體指數更大漲3.14%，那斯達克終場收高1.69%、標普500亦漲1.14%、道瓊小漲0.61%，科技七巨頭同步走高，輝達、特斯拉、亞馬遜漲超2%，微軟、蘋果、Meta、谷歌均漲超1%。

AI硬體與半導體股為主要領漲族群，Arm漲超8%，英特爾漲超7%，閃迪、AMD漲超6%，美光漲超5%，SK海力士、戴爾、邁威爾漲超4%，希捷、高通漲超2%；光通訊族群則表現分化，邁威爾、康寧、Coherent漲超2%，Lumentum跌近3%。AI雲端算力股CoreWeave跌超4%，因該公司擬私募30億美元、2033年到期可轉換優先票據，初始認購方可追加5億美元，並透過ATM發行最多3500萬股A類股，市場擔憂股權稀釋及可轉債攤薄。
美股中概股則漲跌互現，金龍指數微漲0.16%；海川證券漲25%，燃石醫學漲近8%，小馬智行漲超5%，比亞迪ADR漲超3%，嗶哩嗶哩、美團ADR、拼多多偏弱。
與此同時，中東局勢則增添新的變數。美國網媒《Axios》最新報導指出，美國總統川普正考慮是否對伊朗重啟大規模攻勢，擬下週聯合國大會期間會晤6個波斯灣國家領導人，決定外交降溫或軍事升級。
部分美國官員警告，美伊衝突陷「非戰非和」僵局，若談判無果，期中選舉後恐恢復大規模作戰。油價回落與軍事升級預期拉扯，料繼續影響能源、黃金及科技股風險定價。
paras_en: U.S. equities all rose on Thursday (the 17th), with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumping 3.14%. The Nasdaq closed up 1.69%, the S&P 500 gained 1.14% and the Dow slipped 0.61%. The seven big tech names all moved higher – Nvidia, Tesla and Amazon each rose more than 2%, while Microsoft, Apple, Meta and Google each added over 1%.

AI hardware and semiconductor stocks led the gains. Arm surged more than 8%, Intel climbed over 7%, and SanDisk and AMD each rose more than 6%. Micron jumped over 5%, SK Hynix, Dell and Marvell each added more than 4%, and Seagate and Qualcomm were up over 2%. In the optical‑communications sector performance was mixed: Marvell, Corning and Coherent each rose more than 2% while Lumentum fell nearly 3%. Cloud‑AI compute provider CoreWeave dropped more than 4% after it announced a $3 billion private placement of convertible preferred notes due 2033, with the initial investors allowed to add $500 million and the company planning to issue up to 35 million Class A shares via an ATM, sparking concerns about dilution and bond‑conversion dilution.

Chinese‑listed U.S. stocks showed mixed results. The Golden Dragon Index inched up 0.16%. HaiChuan Securities jumped 25%, Burning Rock Medical rose close to 8%, Pony.ai surged over 5%, BYD ADR gained more than 3%, while Bilibili, Meituan ADR and Pinduoduo were weaker.

At the same time, the Middle‑East situation added a new variable. According to a recent report by Axios, former President Donald Trump is weighing whether to restart a large‑scale offensive against Iran and plans to meet leaders of six Persian Gulf countries during next week’s United Nations General Assembly to decide on diplomatic de‑escalation or a military escalation.

Some U.S. officials warned that the U.S.–Iran clash is stuck in a “neither war nor peace” stalemate and that, if negotiations fail, a large‑scale operation could resume after the midterm elections. Falling oil prices and expectations of military escalation are pulling in opposite directions, likely continuing to affect the pricing of energy, gold and technology stocks.

items.title: 英特爾飆近8%、美光漲逾5% 晶片股強勢反彈持續
items.title_en: Intel Soars Nearly 8%, Micron Rises Over 5% as Chip Stocks Continue Strong Rebound
paras: 《MarketWatch》報導，晶片股周四(17日)大幅走高，延續本周初遭遇拋售後的強勁反彈走勢。
英特爾(Intel)(INTC-US)股價周四飆漲7.7%，AI晶片製造商邁威爾(Marvell Technology)(MRVL-US)與超微(Advanced Micro Devices, AMD)(AMD-US)分別上漲4.8%與6.5%。安謀(Arm Holdings)(ARM-US)ADR股價飆升8.6%。
美光(Micron Technology)(MU-US)股價周四上漲5.5%，Sandisk(SNDK-US)股價則勁揚6.2%。
D.A. Davidson總經理Gil Luria表示，油價與美國公債殖利率下滑，可能「消除投資人部分疑慮」。投資人原本在周三聯準會(Fed)會議後產生一些擔憂。Fed決定升息1碼，並為未來至少再升息一次敞開大門。
Luria指出，「資料中心的建設對利率相當敏感，因此任何顯示利率升幅可能不如預期的訊號，對資料中心擴建都是利多，進而也有利於半導體企業。」
晶片類股周一遭遇重挫。此前，包括Anthropic執行長Dario Amodei與OpenAI執行長Sam Altman在內的AI產業領袖，於周末呼籲放慢AI發展速度。部分投資人一度擔心，相關呼籲可能影響AI基礎設施支出。
不過，晶片股及伺服器與零組件製造商的股價從周二開始反彈，因華爾街分析師表示，AI基礎設施擴建背後的基本成長動能依然強勁。
paras_en: MarketWatch reported that chip stocks surged sharply on Thursday (the 17th), continuing the strong rebound after the sell‑off earlier this week.
Intel (INTC-US) jumped 7.7% on Thursday, while AI chip maker Marvell Technology (MRVL-US) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD-US) rose 4.8% and 6.5% respectively. Arm Holdings (ARM-US) ADR surged 8.6%.
Micron Technology (MU-US) gained 5.5% on Thursday, and SanDisk (SNDK-US) rallied 6.2%.
D.A. Davidson Managing Director Gil Luria said that falling oil prices and U.S. Treasury yields could "remove some investors’ concerns," which had arisen after Wednesday’s Federal Reserve meeting.

Luria noted that "data‑center construction is very rate‑sensitive, so any signal that rate hikes may be less than expected is bullish for data‑center expansion and, in turn, for semiconductor companies."

Chip stocks took a heavy hit on Monday. Earlier, AI industry leaders—including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman—called over the weekend for a slowdown in AI development, prompting some investors to worry that the appeals could curb AI infrastructure spending.
However, chip stocks and server and component makers have been rallying since Tuesday, as Wall Street analysts say the underlying growth momentum behind AI infrastructure expansion remains robust.

items.title: 川習會前釋緩和訊號？美國傳延後公布「產能過剩關稅」
items.title_en: Pre‑Summit Signals of Softening? U.S. Said to Delay Announcement of “Overcapacity Tariffs”
paras: 《彭博》週五 (18日) 報導，據知情人士透露，美國政府預計延後公布針對貿易夥伴產能過剩問題的新關稅措施，至少要等到美國總統川普與中國國家主席習近平下週舉行峰會後才會宣布。目前尚不清楚延後公布的原因。
先前報導，川普政府原定在美中領袖峰會前發布產能過剩貿易調查報告，並建議對中國商品加徵 7.5% 關稅。
若依原定稅率實施，川普第二任期對中國商品加徵的關稅水準將恢復至約 20%。
北京先前表示，約 20% 的關稅水準符合美中貿易休戰安排。不過，目前仍不確定最終稅率是否會維持原先規劃的 7.5%。
川普政府今年 3 月依據《1974 年貿易法》第 301 條，針對十多個主要貿易夥伴的產能過剩問題展開調查。
預計推出的產能過剩關稅，加上已實施的強迫勞動相關關稅，最終可望使相關國家的關稅水準，更接近川普原先設定、但今年稍早遭最高法院推翻的國別關稅。
美國貿易代表署與白宮均未回應置評要求。《Inside US Trade》最先披露美方延後公布相關措施的消息。
美國總統川普與大陸國家主席習近平預計24日在華府會面，這將是兩人今年第二次會晤，也將是習近平十年來首次白宮之行，川習會討論主題料將涵蓋貿易、台灣、伊朗問題，以及人工智慧等，。
習近平預計23日晚間抵達美國馬里蘭州安德魯聯合基地，川普將罕見親自前往停機坪接機，給予極高規格的禮遇，24日在白宮與美國總統川普會談，25日便離境。預計習不會出席同期在紐約舉行的聯合國大會。此外，川習今年底前還可能在APEC峰會和G20峰會上會面。
(本文不開放合作夥伴轉載)
paras_en: Bloomberg reported on Friday the 18th that, according to informed sources, the U.S. government plans to postpone the release of new tariff measures aimed at trade partners’ overcapacity problems until after President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping hold their summit next week. The reason for the delay is not yet clear.

Earlier reports said the Trump administration had originally intended to publish an overcapacity trade investigation report before the U.S.–China leaders’ summit and to recommend a 7.5% tariff on Chinese goods.
If the originally proposed rate is applied, the tariff level on Chinese products during Trump’s second term would rise back to roughly 20%.

Beijing previously indicated that a roughly 20% tariff level would be consistent with the U.S.–China trade truce arrangement, but it remains uncertain whether the final rate will stay at the initially planned 7.5%.
In March this year, the Trump administration launched investigations under Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act into overcapacity issues affecting more than a dozen major trading partners.

The anticipated overcapacity tariffs, combined with tariffs already imposed for forced‑labor concerns, are expected to bring the overall tariff levels on the targeted countries closer to the country‑specific rates that Trump originally set but that were overturned by the Supreme Court earlier this year.
Neither the U.S. Trade Representative nor the White House responded to requests for comment. Inside US Trade was the first to reveal the U.S. decision to delay the announcement of the measures.

President Trump and Chinese President Xi are scheduled to meet in Washington on the 24th, marking their second encounter this year and Xi’s first visit to the White House in a decade. The talks are expected to cover trade, Taiwan, Iran, artificial intelligence and other issues.

Xi is expected to arrive on the evening of the 23rd at Andrews Air Force Base in Maryland, where Trump will unusually greet him on the tarmac and extend a high‑level welcome. The two will hold a meeting at the White House on the 24th and Xi will depart on the 25th, likely skipping the United Nations General Assembly in New York. The leaders may also meet later this year at the APEC and G20 summits.

items.title: Arm飆漲8% 20億美元AI晶片銷售目標更近了
items.title_en: Arm Soars 8% as $2 Billion AI Chip Sales Target Comes Closer
paras: 安謀控股(Arm Holdings)(ARM-US)執行長發表樂觀評論，帶動該公司股價周四(17日)躋身那斯達克漲幅最大股票之列。
隨著科技股全面走高，Arm美國掛牌股票周四大漲8.6%。就在一天前，執行長Rene Haas接受CNBC財經節目主持人Jim Cramer採訪時表示，相較於公司5月公布財報時提出20億美元的目標，如今對於旗下首款AI晶片能夠達成該銷售目標「更有信心」。
Haas表示，市場對Arm產品的需求「從未如此強勁」，目前限制公司營收成長的主要因素，將是能否在競爭激烈的AI晶片市場中取得足夠的供應。
長期以來，Arm的主要收入來自晶片設計，相關晶片廣泛應用於智慧型手機，以及包括輝達(NVDA-US)和Alphabet(GOOGL-US)在內的其他科技公司的產品。
面對智慧型手機市場走弱，Arm今年3月宣布計劃開始銷售自有AI晶片。當時公司表示，這款新晶片到2031年可能帶來150億美元營收。
隨著周四股價上漲，Arm美國掛牌股票今年以來累計上漲140%。不過，由於市場對人工智慧支出的可持續性產生疑慮，AI相關股票承壓，Arm目前仍較6月18日創下的歷史高點452.70美元下跌逾40%。
paras_en: Arm Holdings CEO gave optimistic comments, driving the company’s stock to become one of the biggest gainers on Nasdaq on Thursday (the 17th).

With tech stocks broadly rallying, Arm’s US‑listed shares jumped 8.6% on Thursday. Just a day earlier, CEO Rene Haas told CNBC host Jim Cramer that compared with the $2 billion target set when the company released its earnings in May, he is now “more confident” that its first AI chip can achieve that sales goal.

Haas said demand for Arm’s products has “never been this strong,” and the main factor limiting revenue growth now is whether the company can secure enough supply in the fiercely competitive AI chip market.
Historically, Arm’s main revenue comes from chip design, with its chips widely used in smartphones and in products from other tech firms such as Nvidia (NVDA-US) and Alphabet (GOOGL-US).
Facing a weakening smartphone market, Arm announced in March that it would start selling its own AI chip. At that time the company said the new chip could generate $15 billion in revenue by 2031.

With Thursday’s price rise, Arm’s US‑listed shares are up 140% year‑to‑date. However, because of doubts about the sustainability of AI spending, AI‑related stocks are under pressure, and Arm is still down more than 40% from its historic high of $452.70 set on June 18.

items.title: 迪士尼：川普威脅記者 應促法院阻止FCC提前審查ABC執照
items.title_en: Disney: Trump Threatens Reporters, Urges Court to Stop FCC from Early Review of ABC Licenses
paras: 華特迪士尼(Disney) (DIS-US)周四(17日)向美國聯邦法院表示, 川普持續對記者及廣播電視網絡發出威脅, 應足以促使法院阻止聯邦通信委員會(FCC)提前審查迪士尼旗下8家ABC電視台的執照。迪士尼與ABC在最新法院文件中指出,FCC主席布蘭登．卡爾(Brendan Carr)已明確表明, 他正在執行川普針對批評政府言論所提出的具體指示。
迪士尼與ABC表示, 川普針對媒體的公開言論以及FCC後續行動, 已構成政府試圖影響媒體內容的證據。公司主張, 如果FCC繼續推動對8家ABC電視台執照的提前審查, 將使政府能夠利用廣播執照監管權力對媒體施壓, 因此法院應介入阻止相關程序。
這起爭議源自FCC近期對ABC旗下8家電視台執照展開提前審查。按照原有安排, 相關執照並非近期即將到期, 但FCC要求提前啟動程序, 使迪士尼認為此舉與川普對ABC及其節目內容的批評具有直接關聯。
迪士尼在8月已向華盛頓特區聯邦地方法院提起訴訟, 要求阻止FCC提前審查8家ABC電視台執照。迪士尼當時主張, 川普政府正在利用聯邦監管機構向ABC施壓, 要求該電視網改變節目內容, 否則可能面臨廣播執照遭到處理的風險。
川普過去一段時間多次公開批評廣播媒體及部分節目, 並曾要求ABC等廣播電視網停止播出他認為不適當或批評其政府的新聞與娛樂內容。迪士尼因此認為, FCC提前審查ABC執照並非單純的監管程序, 而是與政府對媒體內容施壓的整體行動存在關聯。這些說法屬於迪士尼在訴訟中的主張, 美國政府及FCC則否認其所指控的法律基礎。
FCC主席卡爾曾表示, 迪士尼的訴訟缺乏法律依據。FCC方面主張, 委員會有權調查涉及廣播執照及公共利益義務的問題, 提前啟動執照審查並不等同於對迪士尼施加制裁。
FCC在9月3日向法院提出動議, 要求駁回迪士尼的訴訟。FCC當時表示, 如果迪士尼成功阻止提前審查, 將使委員會無法分析正在進行調查所取得的證據, 並削弱FCC調查及處理相關指控的能力。FCC並指稱, 調查涉及迪士尼是否存在違法歧視等嚴重問題。
美國司法部此前也反對迪士尼要求法院立即召開緊急聽證的請求。司法部表示, FCC如果發布執照審查命令,並不代表立即對迪士尼實施制裁, 而是啟動進一步的行政程序, 屆時迪士尼與ABC仍有機會提出自身主張。FCC也同意在發布相關命令前至少提前48小時通知迪士尼。
迪士尼則認為, 48小時通知並不足以解決其所提出的憲法問題。公司主張, FCC的監管權力如果是受到總統針對特定媒體內容的要求所驅動, 即使尚未正式撤銷廣播執照, 相關政府行動本身仍可能對新聞及言論自由產生寒蟬效應。
最新法院文件中, 迪士尼特別將川普對記者及廣播網絡的持續威脅列為支持其請求的重要理由。公司認為, 這些公開言論與FCC針對ABC採取的監管措施放在一起觀察, 足以支持法院阻止FCC提前審查8家ABC電視台執照。
這起案件也與川普政府及美國媒體之間持續升高的衝突有關。除了ABC執照爭議外, FCC今年也曾對ABC節目「The View」展開調查。迪士尼則認為, 多項監管行動與政府對ABC節目內容的不滿相互連結。
另一方面, 美國國會近期也開始處理政府官員是否可以向私人媒體企業施壓的問題。參議院商務委員會16日以18票對10票通過一項法案, 將限制聯邦政府官員迫使私人企業審查或壓制受第一修正案保護的言論。該法案仍須經參議院全院及眾議院審議, 才可能成為法律。
這項國會行動顯示, FCC與ABC之間的爭議已從單純的廣播執照監管問題, 延伸至美國憲法第一修正案所保障的言論自由及政府與私人媒體關係。支持法案的共和黨及民主黨參議員均表示, 政府官員不應利用行政權力迫使私人企業壓制受保護的言論。
目前法院尚未就迪士尼要求阻止FCC提前審查8家ABC電視台執照的最新主張作出最終裁決。案件後續關鍵將包括法院是否認定FCC的行動具有不當政府施壓性質, 以及FCC所提出的廣播執照監管與調查理由是否足以支持提前審查程序。
對迪士尼而言, 這場訴訟的核心不只是8家ABC電視台的執照問題, 而是政府能否因為不滿媒體報導或節目內容, 透過廣播執照及監管機制對媒體企業施加壓力。對FCC及美國政府而言, 則是委員會是否仍可依法調查廣播業者可能涉及的執照及公共利益問題。雙方目前對相關行動的法律性質存在明顯分歧, 最終仍有待法院判決。
paras_en: Disney (DIS-US) told a U.S. federal court on Thursday (17) that Trump’s ongoing threats to reporters and broadcast networks should be enough to compel the court to block the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) from conducting an early review of the licenses of Disney’s eight ABC television stations. Disney and ABC, in the latest court filing, noted that FCC Chair Brendan Carr has made it clear that he is carrying out Trump’s specific directives aimed at criticism of the government.

Disney and ABC argue that Trump’s public statements about the media and the FCC’s subsequent actions constitute evidence that the government is attempting to influence media content. The company contends that if the FCC continues to push for an early review of the eight ABC station licenses, the government would be able to use its broadcast‑licensing regulatory power to pressure the media, and therefore the court should intervene to halt the process.

The dispute stems from the FCC’s recent decision to initiate an early review of the eight ABC station licenses. Under the original schedule, the licenses were not due to expire soon, but the FCC demanded that the process be started early, which Disney sees as directly linked to Trump’s criticism of ABC and its programming.

In August, Disney filed a lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia seeking to stop the FCC’s early review of the eight ABC station licenses. Disney then argued that the Trump administration was using federal regulatory agencies to pressure ABC to change its programming, or else risk having its broadcast license revoked.

Trump has repeatedly publicly criticized broadcast media and certain programs, and has asked networks such as ABC to stop airing what he considers inappropriate or critical content. Disney therefore believes that the FCC’s early review of ABC licenses is not a simple regulatory procedure but is part of a broader effort by the government to pressure media content. These claims are part of Disney’s litigation; the U.S. government and the FCC deny the legal basis of the allegations.

FCC Chair Carr has said that Disney’s lawsuit lacks legal grounds. The FCC maintains that it has the authority to investigate matters involving broadcast licenses and public‑interest obligations, and that initiating an early review does not equate to sanctioning Disney.

On September 3, the FCC filed a motion with the court to dismiss Disney’s lawsuit. The FCC argued that if Disney succeeds in stopping the early review, the commission would be unable to analyze evidence gathered in the ongoing investigation, thereby weakening its ability to investigate and address related allegations. The FCC also alleged that the investigation concerns serious issues such as whether Disney is engaging in unlawful discrimination.

The U.S. Department of Justice has also opposed Disney’s request for an emergency hearing. The DOJ said that an FCC license‑review order does not constitute an immediate sanction against Disney, but merely initiates further administrative procedures, at which point Disney and ABC would still have the opportunity to present their case. The FCC agreed to give Disney at least 48 hours’ notice before issuing any related order.

Disney argues that a 48‑hour notice is insufficient to address the constitutional issues it raises. The company contends that if the FCC’s regulatory power is driven by presidential requests targeting specific media content, even if a broadcast license has not yet been formally revoked, the government action itself could have a chilling effect on news and free speech.

In the latest court filing, Disney specifically cites Trump’s ongoing threats to reporters and broadcast networks as a key reason supporting its request. The company believes that these public statements, viewed alongside the FCC’s regulatory actions against ABC, are sufficient to justify a court order to block the early review of the eight ABC station licenses.

The case is also tied to the escalating conflict between the Trump administration and U.S. media. In addition to the ABC license dispute, the FCC investigated ABC’s program "The View" this year. Disney argues that multiple regulatory actions are interconnected with the government’s dissatisfaction with ABC’s programming.

Meanwhile, Congress has recently begun addressing whether government officials can pressure private media companies. On the 16th, the Senate Commerce Committee passed a bill 18‑to‑10 to restrict federal officials from forcing private firms to review or suppress First‑Amendment‑protected speech. The bill still requires approval by the full Senate and the House before it can become law.

This congressional action shows that the dispute between the FCC and ABC has expanded from a simple broadcast‑licensing issue to one involving First‑Amendment free‑speech protections and the relationship between government and private media. Republican and Democratic senators supporting the bill say officials should not use executive power to compel private firms to suppress protected speech.

The court has not yet issued a final ruling on Disney’s latest claim to block the FCC’s early review of the eight ABC station licenses. Key issues moving forward include whether the court will find the FCC’s actions to be improper government pressure, and whether the FCC’s stated regulatory and investigative reasons justify the early‑review procedure.

For Disney, the core of this lawsuit is not merely the licenses of the eight ABC stations but whether the government can use broadcast licensing and regulatory mechanisms to pressure media companies over dissatisfaction with reporting or programming. For the FCC and the U.S. government, the question is whether the commission can still lawfully investigate potential licensing and public‑interest issues involving broadcasters. Both sides currently have starkly different views on the legal nature of the actions, and the final outcome remains to be decided by the court.

items.title: 日本10年債殖利率飆破3% 貝森特「逼宮」日本大撒錢 要求升息、收斂財政支出
items.title_en: Japan 10-Year Bond Yield Surges Past 3% as Bessent Pressures Tokyo to Spend Big, Demand Rate Hikes and Fiscal Tightening
paras: 美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)近幾個月持續向日本政府施壓，要求東京控制大規模財政支出、讓日本央行加快升息，以遏制日元疲弱與通膨壓力。路透引述3名知情人士指出，當日本財務大臣片山皐月(Satsuki Katayama)今年6月22日致電貝森特，希望美國協助支撐大幅走貶的日元時，貝森特反而要求日本先處理財政政策問題，並避免貨幣與財政政策相互矛盾。
這通此前未被公開報導的電話，成為美日兩國7月底大規模聯手干預匯市的前奏。日本方面原本擔心日元疲弱推高通膨，進而傷害首相高市早苗的政治支持度；但貝森特更關注日本公債遭大幅拋售可能波及美國公債市場。日本是美國國債最大的海外持有國，因此日本長期公債殖利率若大幅攀升，可能推高美國政府的借貸成本。
貝森特過去數月已私下向片山及其他日本官員表示，日本應收斂大規模財政支出，同時日本央行需要升息。他在6月通話中再次要求東京處理推低日元的根本因素，並認為高市政府擴大支出的政策，正在削弱日本央行抑制通膨的努力。
貝森特5月在日本與片山會面時，也曾強調日本央行需要提高利率。3名消息人士表示，當時日本政府內部已普遍認為6月或7月升息幾乎勢在必行。日本央行6月升息後，片山一度認為貝森特可能同意美國加入聯合買進日元的行動，但貝森特仍把焦點放在日本財政政策。
7月底，美日最終展開聯合干預匯市。日本首席外匯事務官三村淳(Atsushi Mimura)當時形容，這是日本與美國貨幣合作關係的成果。日本財務省與美國財政部的合作，使日元一度明顯反彈，但這波升值並未持續太久。
數周後，日元重新走弱，美國方面對高市政府未能明顯撤回刺激經濟措施感到失望，加上全球公債殖利率同步攀升，使日本財政問題受到更大關注。8月31日至9月1日舉行的G20財長會議上，貝森特再次要求日本升息並收緊財政政策，且語氣較先前更為強硬。
貝森特此前接受媒體訪問時表示，日本應該「坐下來享受安倍經濟學的成功」，理由是日本長期通縮時代已經過去，目前政策重點應從刺激經濟轉向控制通膨。這被視為美國迄今對高市政府延續安倍經濟學政策最明確的警告之一。
隨著市場持續拋售日本公債，日本10年期基準公債殖利率9月初升破3%關卡，觸及30年高點。日本前最高外匯事務官古澤滿宏(Mitsuhiro Furusawa)指出，日本公共債務規模龐大，需要提出可信的中長期財政展望，並確保貨幣政策與財政政策一致，避免長期利率出現不受歡迎的急升。
在G20會議期間，片山向與會財長保證，日本將降低對額外支出的依賴，也不會透過發行債券來支應減稅。她會後透露，自己曾向貝森特展示高市早苗接受日本媒體《讀賣新聞》訪問時提出的「同時實現經濟成長與財政紀律」主張，貝森特則回應表示認同。
貝森特隨後再度對日元空頭發出警告，並表示自己掌握部分日本政策制定者包括日本央行的非對稱資訊，對政策走向具有較深入的了解。他甚至表示「現在我是莊家」，並稱投資人如果願意可以押注與他相反的方向，相關言論也一度帶動日元升值。
這場美日財政與貨幣政策角力，正值日本央行準備進一步升息之際。日本央行的政策方向大致與貝森特要求提高利率的立場一致，但在財政政策方面，日本政府與美國之間仍存在明顯落差。
高市早苗很難完全撤回帶動其所屬政黨在今年選舉中取得支持的主要刺激政策。政府透過補貼及其他措施降低燃料成本，也有助於緩解民眾對生活成本上升的不滿，因此大幅削減支出可能帶來政治壓力。
另一方面，美國若要求日本大幅縮減減稅與支出計畫，也可能削弱一個重要亞洲盟友的政府穩定性。在美國與中國競爭升溫之際，華府仍重視與日本的安全及經濟合作。美國總統川普在美日共同支撐日元後，也再次強調兩國夥伴關係的重要性。
日本政府周四進行內閣改組，高市早苗重新任命片山皐月擔任財務大臣，被部分市場人士視為兼顧市場信心與政策延續性的安排。片山本身較偏向財政保守立場，近來一方面需要向市場保證日本不會無限制擴大支出，另一方面也必須推動高市政府的投資與經濟政策。
不過，目前並沒有跡象顯示高市政府準備全面放棄擴張性財政政策。日本下一財政年度的預算要求總額已膨脹至143兆日元(約9,161.4億美元)，接近疫情期間的高峰。高市政府則承諾，在截至2028年3月的財政年度，新發行公債規模將維持約40兆日元，高於本年度預估的32.7兆日元。
部分日本官員認為，若考量臨時調降消費稅、增加國防支出以及融資成本上升，要將新發債規模控制在40兆日元左右可能相當困難。日本政府近期公布的食品消費稅減免計畫本身就可能造成約5兆日元的稅收缺口，進一步增加市場對財政健全性的疑慮。
目前這場財政政策僵局尚未演變成更大規模的美日衝突，顯示高市政府與川普政府之間仍保有一定外交空間。不過，部分分析人士認為，貝森特對日本財政政策的施壓，反映川普政府正在把其對盟友的談判方式延伸至金融與財政政策領域。
日本前外匯官員中尾武彥(Takehiko Nakao)表示，美國過去對日本的訊息較偏向要求東京採取正確政策，如今則顯得更直接。美國關切的不只是日元匯率，也包括日本公債市場穩定、通膨政策可信度，以及日本大量持有美國國債對美國融資成本可能造成的影響。
因此，貝森特與日本政府之間的角力已不再只是單純的匯率問題，而是同時牽涉日本央行升息速度、政府支出、減稅、國防預算、日本公債殖利率，以及全球最大兩個政府債券市場之間的相互影響。對高市政府而言，如何在維持經濟刺激政策、控制生活成本與回應金融市場對財政紀律的要求之間取得平衡，將成為後續政策的核心課題。
paras_en: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been pressing the Japanese government for months, urging Tokyo to curb massive fiscal spending and accelerate rate hikes by the Bank of Japan to curb a weak yen and inflation pressures. Reuters, citing three informed sources, said that when Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama called Bessent on June 22 to ask for U.S. support for the sharply depreciating yen, Bessent instead told Japan to first address its fiscal policy issues and avoid contradictions between monetary and fiscal policy.

The previously undisclosed call set the stage for the large‑scale joint FX intervention by the United States and Japan at the end of July. Japan had feared that a weak yen would lift inflation and erode Prime Minister Kishida Nae‑suke’s political support, but Bessent was more worried that a heavy sell‑off of Japanese government bonds could spill over into the U.S. Treasury market. Japan is the largest foreign holder of U.S. Treasuries, so a sharp rise in Japanese long‑term bond yields could push up borrowing costs for the U.S. government.

Bessent has privately told Katayama and other Japanese officials over the past few months that Japan should rein in its massive fiscal outlays while the BOJ needs to raise rates. In the June call he again urged Tokyo to tackle the root causes of yen weakness and argued that the Kishida administration’s expansionary spending was undermining the BOJ’s fight against inflation.

When Bessent met Katayama in Japan in May, he also stressed that the BOJ needed to hike rates. Three sources said that at the time the Japanese government already believed a rate hike in June or July was almost inevitable. After the BOJ raised rates in June, Katayama briefly thought Bessent might agree to a joint yen‑buying operation, but Bessent kept the focus on Japan’s fiscal stance.

At the end of July the U.S. and Japan carried out a joint FX intervention. Japan’s chief foreign exchange official Atsushi Mimura described it as the fruit of monetary cooperation between the two countries. The coordination between Japan’s finance ministry and the U.S. Treasury sparked a noticeable yen rally, but the appreciation was short‑lived.

Weeks later the yen weakened again. The United States expressed disappointment that the Kishida government had not rolled back its stimulus measures, and rising global bond yields heightened scrutiny of Japan’s fiscal situation. At the G20 finance ministers’ meeting on Aug. 31‑Sept. 1, Bessent again demanded that Japan raise rates and tighten fiscal policy, using a tougher tone than before.

In a prior media interview Bessent said Japan should “sit down and enjoy the success of Abenomics,” arguing that the era of chronic deflation is over and policy should shift from stimulus to inflation control. The comment was seen as one of the clearest U.S. warnings to the Kishida administration about continuing Abenomics‑style policies.

As markets kept selling Japanese bonds, the yield on the benchmark 10‑year Japanese government bond broke the 3% barrier in early September, hitting a 30‑year high. Former top FX official Mitsuhiro Furusawa warned that Japan’s huge public debt requires a credible medium‑ to long‑term fiscal outlook and alignment of monetary and fiscal policy to avoid an unwelcome surge in long‑term rates.

During the G20 meeting Katayama assured fellow finance chiefs that Japan would reduce reliance on extra spending and would not fund tax cuts by issuing new bonds. After the meeting she disclosed that she had shown Bessent Kishida’s “grow the economy while maintaining fiscal discipline” pitch given to Yomiuri Shimbun, which Bessent said he agreed with.

Bessent later warned yen short‑sellers again, claiming he possessed asymmetric information about Japanese policymakers, including the BOJ, giving him deeper insight into policy direction. He even said, “Now I am the house,” and suggested investors could bet against him, a remark that briefly boosted the yen.

The U.S.–Japan clash over fiscal and monetary policy comes as the BOJ prepares to raise rates further. The BOJ’s policy trajectory broadly aligns with Bessent’s call for higher rates, but a gap remains on the fiscal side between Japan’s government and Washington.

Kishida finds it hard to fully roll back the stimulus measures that have helped his party gain electoral support this year. Subsidies and other actions that lower fuel costs ease public anger over rising living expenses, so a sharp cut in spending could create political pressure.

Conversely, if the United States demands a major cut in Japan’s tax cuts and spending plans, it could undermine the stability of an important Asian ally. With U.S.–China competition heating up, Washington still values Japan’s security and economic partnership. After the joint effort to support the yen, President Trump again stressed the importance of the bilateral partnership.

Japan reshuffled its cabinet on Thursday, re‑appointing Katayama as finance minister under Kishida, a move some market participants saw as balancing market confidence with policy continuity. Katayama leans fiscally conservative and now must reassure markets that Japan will not expand spending unchecked while still advancing Kishida’s investment and economic agenda.

Nevertheless, there is no sign that the Kishida administration is ready to abandon its expansionary fiscal stance. The budget request for the next fiscal year has swelled to ¥143 trillion (about $9.16 billion), near the pandemic‑era peak. The government has pledged that new bond issuance for the fiscal year ending March 2028 will stay around ¥40 trillion, above the current‑year estimate of ¥32.7 trillion.

Some officials argue that, given a temporary cut to the consumption tax, higher defence spending and rising financing costs, keeping new issuance near ¥40 trillion will be very difficult. The recently announced food‑tax relief plan could create a ¥5 trillion revenue gap, further raising doubts about fiscal soundness.

The fiscal standoff has not yet escalated into a broader U.S.–Japan clash, indicating that diplomatic space remains between the Kishida and Trump administrations. However, some analysts say Bessent’s pressure on Japan’s fiscal policy reflects the Trump administration’s habit of extending its negotiating style with allies into financial and fiscal realms.

Former FX official Takehiko Nakao said the United States used to mainly tell Tokyo to adopt the right policies, but now its messaging is more direct. Washington’s concerns cover not only the yen rate but also the stability of Japan’s bond market, the credibility of its inflation policy and the impact of Japan’s large U.S. Treasury holdings on U.S. financing costs.

Thus the contest between Bessent and the Japanese government is no longer just about exchange rates; it also involves BOJ rate‑hike speed, government spending, tax cuts, defence budgeting, Japanese bond yields and the interaction of the world’s two largest sovereign‑debt markets. For Kishida’s government, balancing economic stimulus, cost‑of‑living pressures and market demands for fiscal discipline will be the core policy challenge going forward.

items.title: 植田談話恐令市場失望？日銀利率決議出爐前夕　富國銀行高調做空日元、花旗估將跌向159
items.title_en: Will Ueda's Remarks Disappoint the Market? On the Eve of the BOJ Rate Decision, Wells Fargo Shorts the Yen Aggressively, Citi Forecasts a Drop to 159
paras: 日本央行(BOJ)公布最新利率決議前夕，外匯策略師普遍預期「升息容易、表態難鷹」，日元短線偏向貶值。掉期市場數據幾乎完全計入升息1碼，焦點轉向BOJ總裁植田和男記者會對後續節奏的指引。日元在今日亞洲匯市早盤小貶約0.1%至156.15。
富國銀行策略師Chidu Narayanan表示，BOJ要達到甚至超越市場鷹派預期「門檻​​很高」，會議結果若僅兌現升息、不明示連續緊縮，風險傾向偏鴿，建議做空日元。
ING Bank NV的G10外匯策略主管Chris Turner預估，若BOJ未能釋放進一步升息訊號，日元兌美元將貶至157或158水平，花旗策略師Daniel Tobon更預估未來幾週日元可能貶向159。
壓低日元反彈的是美日利差。聯準會(Fed)週三宣布升息1碼至3.75%—4%，主席華許暗示通膨偏高、必要時繼續收緊，美元指數站上100，美債短端利率走高，
不過，策略師們對中長線判斷分化；花旗認為日本近期匯率與貨幣政策調整屬「制度轉變」一部分，長期仍利於日元；荷蘭銀行資深外匯策略師Georgette Boele則預期能源價格暫時抑制反彈，2027年第一季前美元兌日元將在154附近交易，2027下半年隨Fed、歐洲央行(ECB)降息才轉強。整體來看，短線市場以「鴿派升息」防日元回貶，158—160為關鍵觀察區。
paras_en: Ahead of the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) latest rate decision, most FX strategists expect a "rate hike is easy, hawkish guidance is hard," implying short‑term yen weakness. Swap market data almost fully priced in a 10‑basis‑point hike, shifting focus to the guidance on future pacing from BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda's press conference. The yen slipped about 0.1% to 156.15 in early Asian trading today.

Wells Fargo strategist Chidu Narayanan said the BOJ faces a very high hurdle to meet or exceed market hawkish expectations. If the meeting only delivers a hike without signalling further tightening, the bias leans dovish, so he recommends shorting the yen.

ING Bank NV’s G10 FX strategy head Chris Turner projected that if the BOJ fails to signal additional hikes, the yen will fall to the 157‑158 level against the dollar, while Citi strategist Daniel Tobon sees the yen possibly sliding toward 159 in the coming weeks.

The yen’s downside is being capped by the US‑Japan rate differential. The Fed raised rates by one quarter point on Wednesday to a 3.75%‑4% range, with Chair Powell hinting that inflation remains elevated and further tightening may be needed. The dollar index is above 100 and short‑term US Treasury yields are rising.

However, strategists diverge on the medium‑to‑long term. Citi views Japan’s recent exchange‑rate and policy moves as part of a "structural shift" that will ultimately benefit the yen, while senior ING FX strategist Georgette Boele expects energy prices to temporarily suppress a rebound, forecasting the dollar‑yen around 154 before Q1 2027 and only strengthening in the second half of 2027 after rate cuts by the Fed and ECB. Overall, the short‑term market is watching the "dovish hike" narrative to prevent a yen rebound, with 158‑160 as the key observation zone.

items.title: 聯準會升息後美股反而大漲那斯達克漲1.7%、英特爾AMD領軍晶片股反攻
items.title_en: U.S. Stocks Surge After Fed Rate Hike, Nasdaq Up 1.7% as Intel, AMD Lead Chip Rally
paras: 2026年09月18日（優分析／產業數據中心報導）⸺ 美國聯準會升息1碼後，美股週四出現明顯反彈，那斯達克指數上漲1.7%，重新站上50日均線，同時收復10日與21日均線；標普500指數上漲1.1%，道瓊工業指數則上漲0.6%。市場情緒改善之際，半導體股成為主要領漲族群。
債券殖利率回落也舒緩成長股估值壓力，美國10年期公債殖利率下跌超過6個基點至4.94%。那斯達克成交量較前一交易日增加，上漲家數超過下跌家數2倍，顯示反彈並非集中於少數大型科技股。
半導體族群漲勢尤其突出，VanEck Semiconductor ETF上漲2.8%。英特爾Intel(INTC-US)大漲近8%，超微AMD(AMD-US)上漲逾6%；記憶體與儲存族群同步走強，SanDisk(SNDK-US)上漲6%，美光Micron Technology(MU-US)上漲5.5%。
道瓊成分股方面，輝達NVIDIA(NVDA-US)、思科Cisco Systems(CSCO-US)與亞馬遜Amazon(AMZN-US)均上漲逾2%。小型半導體股也跟進反彈，Penguin Solutions(PENG-US)與MaxLinear(MXL-US)漲幅達8%至9%。
AI資料中心電力設備則出現更強烈的個股反應。Generac Holdings(GNRC-US)大漲18%，成為標普500指數表現最強個股，主因公司與亞馬遜簽署長期協議，將為亞馬遜資料中心供應發電機。

In semiconductors, Arm Holdings (ARM-US) jumped 8.6%. CEO Rene Haas said the company’s confidence has grown in securing sufficient supply to meet a $2 billion data‑center chip demand. AMD (AMD-US), Intel (INTC-US), Marvell Technology (MRVL-US), Coherent (COHR-US), Corning (GLW-US) and SanDisk (SNDK-US) also moved higher.

By contrast, energy‑storage firm Fluence Energy (FLNC-US) slid more than 15% after a delay in ramp‑up at its outsourced manufacturing plant in Houston forced a sharp downward revision of its FY 2026 revenue outlook. paras_en: Bloomberg reported on Friday the 18th that, according to informed sources, the U.S. government plans to postpone the release of new tariff measures aimed at trade partners’ overcapacity problems until after President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping hold their summit next week. The reason for the delay is not yet clear.

Earlier reports said the Trump administration had originally intended to publish an overcapacity trade investigation report before the U.S.–China leaders’ summit and to recommend a 7.5% tariff on Chinese goods.
If the originally proposed rate is applied, the tariff level on Chinese products during Trump’s second term would rise back to roughly 20%.

Beijing previously indicated that a roughly 20% tariff level would be consistent with the U.S.–China trade truce arrangement, but it remains uncertain whether the final rate will stay at the initially planned 7.5%.
In March this year, the Trump administration launched investigations under Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act into overcapacity issues affecting more than a dozen major trading partners.

The anticipated overcapacity tariffs, combined with tariffs already imposed for forced‑labor concerns, are expected to bring the overall tariff levels on the targeted countries closer to the country‑specific rates that Trump originally set but that were overturned by the Supreme Court earlier this year.
Neither the U.S. Trade Representative nor the White House responded to requests for comment. Inside US Trade was the first to reveal the U.S. decision to delay the announcement of the measures.

President Trump and Chinese President Xi are scheduled to meet in Washington on the 24th, marking their second encounter this year and Xi’s first visit to the White House in a decade. The talks are expected to cover trade, Taiwan, Iran, artificial intelligence and other issues.

Xi is expected to arrive on the evening of the 23rd at Andrews Air Force Base in Maryland, where Trump will unusually greet him on the tarmac and extend a high‑level welcome. The two will hold a meeting at the White House on the 24th and Xi will depart on the 25th, likely skipping the United Nations General Assembly in New York. The leaders may also meet later this year at the APEC and G20 summits.
